name: CT-01
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+12 partisan lean in a Democratic-leaning state
Luke Bronin's large fundraising advantage ($3.1M vs $21K) and outside support
Prediction markets price Democratic win at 96%
Open seat after Larson lost renomination, removing incumbency cushion
model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly Democratic: a D+12 district, a well-funded nominee in Bronin who has raised over $3 million against a Republican with negligible resources, and markets pricing a Democratic win at 96%. With no polls or expert ratings available, the forecast stays close to the fundamentals-based margin of roughly 20 points.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending against Bronin or an unusually favorable Republican national environment could narrow the margin, though a seat this lean is unlikely to flip.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: John B. Larson (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Connecticut's 1st District is an open seat after long incumbent John Larson lost renomination, but the district's D+12 partisan lean keeps it firmly on the Democratic side of the map. Hartford-area voters have consistently elected Democrats, and no expert rating services flag the race as competitive.

Democrat Luke Bronin, a former Hartford mayor, has raised about $3.1 million and enjoys roughly $1.4 million in outside support, while Republican Amy Chai has raised about $21,000 with almost no cash on hand. Prediction markets give the Democrat roughly a 96% chance of winning. The main uncertainty is the absence of polling in an open-seat contest, which widens uncertainty without changing the expected outcome.
